newsitem.title: UK: Schroders posts record profit but shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Schroders posts record profit but shares fall.

text.p: British investment bank Schroders Plc on Wednesday reported record profits but warned it would be a hard act to follow.

"The record results achieved in 1996 will not be easy to repeat in 1997, although there has been an encouraging start to the year," said chairman Win Bischoff after announcing pre-tax profits of 238.7 million pounds ($383 million) compared with 197.3 million in 1995.

This was at the top of analysts' forecasts but led to a fall in Schroders' share price amid concerns over higher costs and below-expectations input from merchant banking. They were down 17.5 pence at 1720 pence in early afternoon but had earlier dropped as low as 1686p.
Schroders' vice-chairman Peter Sedgwick said the group, which announced an increased total dividend of 20 pence, was working on improving investment and merchant banking returns.

"Our objective is to see...returns from that business improve," Sedgwick told Reuters, adding that the bank had been through a year of "very substantial structural changes" and had built up and invested in its securities business.
Sedgwick denied this was the reason for an increase in costs. "The increase in costs is not down to securities, it is across the board."
He said there had been some restructuring of the group's corporate finance business in South East Asia and expansion in Spain and Germany.

"We have been integrating corporate finance with securities throughout the world...we are looking for what has been taking place in the last year to pay off for us to a greater extent over the next year or two," he added.
But he felt the investment and merchant banking side of the business "has performed reasonably well against the changes in strategy that have been taking place here".

The bulk of the cost of this strategy change had been borne in 1996 and costs are not expected to rise in the same way this year. Other factors driving up costs had been increased volumes, regulation and competitive staff conditions.
Staff costs per employee rose to 93,300 pounds from 78,500 the previous year although Schroders' cost/income ratio was 75 percent, compared to 75.4 pct in 1995.

He said Schroders' profits were up by over 20 percent but bonuses had risen slightly below this. Spiralling bonuses in the industry as a whole were, he said, the result of a battle going on between major investment banking players to be one of five or six global powerhouses.
"Sooner or later the damage that some will suffer (means) they will withdraw and the cycle will change," he said, adding that Schroders did not count itself among this group.

Schroders posted a 42 percent rise in pre-tax profits for its asset management business and an 18 percent increase in assets under management. Sedgwick said this was a good performance in line with previous improvements.

Others were desperate to get asset management but Schroders was not attempting to become a Merrill Lynch or a Goldman Sachs and would continue to focus on being an "advisory-relationship type investment bank".

Commenting on long-standing speculation that Schroders could be involved in a merger or takeover by a larger firm, Sedgwick said "There is absolutely no intention of changing Schroders as is. We are not up for sale, we are not out for a merger, we do not want a big brother and we are not in the acquisition stakes".
"We are not in the business of losing our independence," he said, adding that Schroders would grow organically. ($ = 0.623 British Pounds)
